title: LEOPOLD LIQUIDATED LIVE: Ken Griffin is The Grim Reaper, Uniswap V4 Hooks, and a Postmortem
summary:
A wild market day driven by hedge fund manager Leopold Aschenbrenner's fund reportedly getting margin-called and unwinding its book, sending "Leopold stocks" crashing then violently ripping back, while crypto quietly set up for what the host called one of the best entries in a long time.

- **Leopold blowup** — Reports (via FT) said Leopold Aschenbrenner's situational-awareness fund, up 439% through June but using up to 4x leverage with Anthropic as ~50% of the book, sought fresh capital from investors after sharp AI-stock losses. [0:01]
- **Leopold-linked stocks crushed** — Bloom Energy, Nebius, SK Hynix, and other AI/semis names tied to the fund were down 50-60% pre-open, with South Korea reportedly holding emergency meetings over the crash. [5:06]
- **Crypto setup called strong** — Despite the stock carnage, host argued Bitcoin, pump.fun fees, BNB coin, and a Uniswap-v4-style setup showed early "animal spirits" returning to on-chain markets. [1:05]
- **Robinhood/Cash Cat moment** — During Robinhood's earnings event, Cash Cat appeared as the only searched coin on a screen-share, which the host called a well-timed, near-perfect "soft shill." [8:14]
- **Market open reversal** — Stocks opened sharply green (S&P +1%, semis/Nasdaq surging), and previously hammered Leopold-linked names like Bloom Energy, Nebius, Micron and SanDisk snapped back 20-30%. [10:29]
- **Forced liquidation reported** — News broke that Aschenbrenner's fund was unwinding trades and sold its entire public equities book (long and short) to a single buyer, sparking speculation the buyer was Citadel/Ken Griffin. [17:07]
- **Dwarkesh blog theory** — Host floated an unconfirmed, self-described "conspiracy" that Dwarkesh Patel's bullish AI blog post was timed to help bail out his roommate Aschenbrenner, while noting Gavin Baker reacted skeptically to the post. [21:52]

title: I Predicted Leopold Aschenbrenner's $45B Blow Up
summary:
The episode covers a rapid-fire, meme-fueled market saga in which AI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund reportedly blew up and got liquidated, with the hosts reacting live to breaking headlines and tying it to a Dwarkesh Patel blog post.

- **Leopold liquidation story** — Reports say Leopold Aschenbrenner's $24B fund unwound its entire public equities book (longs and shorts) after big AI stock losses and a bad long-semis/short-software bet, reportedly selling to a single buyer. [2:47]
- **Ken Griffin/Citadel angle** — The hosts joke-narrate a theory that Citadel's Ken Griffin drove a rate-hike scare, triggered Leopold's margin call, then bought his entire book at the bottom before the market ran back up. [4:39]
- **Prime broker involvement** — Coverage noted Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan were working with the fund to meet margin requirements or reduce positions in an orderly way. [4:04]
- **Market carnage watched live** — Hosts reacted to huge swings in Nebius, SK Hynix, and Bloom Energy as the "forced seller" news broke, calling it a brutal, out-of-nowhere collapse. [3:17]
- **Dwarkesh Patel blog post** — They found a new Dwarkesh Patel post (via Gavin Baker) about AI labs hitting $1 trillion revenue, and were shocked/amused to spot a typo in a rushed "2-hour timeboxed" bull post timed right before market open. [5:15]
- **Not gloating, but calling it** — One host insisted he wasn't trying to rage-bait or victory-lap Leopold's blowup, saying he felt bad about the size of the losses but was just reporting what happened after correctly calling part of the move. [8:20]

title: Flood - Inside the Biggest AI Fund Blowup Ever
summary:
The episode is an emergency stream breaking down the sudden collapse of Leopold Aschenbrenner's "Situational Awareness" hedge fund and what it revealed about leverage, market structure, and the AI-trade top.

- **Fund blowup explained** — Guest Flood detailed how Leopold's fund went from $500M to a peak NAV around $45B using heavy leverage on concentrated AI/memory-chip positions (Bloom Energy, SanDisk, Nvidia, Micron, SK Hynix), including using illiquid Anthropic equity as loan collateral. [1:14]
- **Margin call and forced sale** — As markets moved against him and volatility spiked, Goldman issued urgent margin calls he couldn't meet; Jane Street (an LP) refused to bail him out, forcing a distressed sale process among big firms like Citadel and Millennium. [16:00]
- **Citadel's "Grim Reaper" trade** — Citadel ultimately bought the liquidated portfolio at a steep discount, a move Flood compared to Ken Griffin's history of buying distressed books (Enron, Amaranth, and reportedly trying with AQR), calling it Citadel's signature sharky trade. [8:22]
- **Why leverage killed him** — Flood argued Leopold's thesis on AI/AGI was directionally correct and he was briefly a top-five trader, but oversized, highly leveraged single-name positions (~20% of market cap) made him vulnerable to being "hunted" once the market sensed forced selling. [11:21]
- **Their own memory short** — Flood's fund held a multi-week short on memory-chip names, funded profitably via Hyperliquid funding rates rather than costly borrows/options, betting the AI/memory rally was overextended and crypto traders lacked real equities edge. [31:02]
- **CapEx skepticism** — Flood said hyperscaler spending hasn't shown up as real revenue/efficiency gains outside of recursive cloud deals with OpenAI/Anthropic, and expects markets to keep punishing companies for high CapEx without visible payoff. [40:05]
- **Current positioning** — The fund is about 50% cash, still holds Bitcoin and Hyperliquid (hedged via short derivatives for tax efficiency, not necessarily bearish), and is watching for further downside before redeploying. [42:37]

title: The Ansem Interview, the Semiconductor Crash, and the LeBron Economy
summary:
The episode covered a brutal market selloff across chips, AI stocks and crypto, plus a live interview with trader Ansem about crypto's future.

- **Kimchi/Burry framing** — Host opened discussing why traders like Kimchi and Michael Burry become celebrated for single huge trades (Kimchi's Trump coin win, Burry's short positions), calling it "folklore" built around one big score. [1:35]
- **Market open carnage** — At open, SPX and Nasdaq were down modestly but semiconductors (SOX down ~4%), DRAM, and Korean KOSPI (down 11%, circuit-broken) were getting crushed; Bitcoin flirted with new lows near $63k. [6:32]
- **Chip/AI stock rout** — Micron, AMD, Intel, Dell, Sandisk, Marvell, ASML, SK Hynix and other AI/memory names were down 5-9%, with Palantir down six and Oracle's chart called one of the worst ever; Tesla hit its cheapest level since August. [10:18]
- **Green pockets** — Amid the rout, Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, Netflix, IBM and PayPal (post-earnings beat) traded green, while crypto-adjacent names like Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle and Strategy sold off hard. [12:25]
- **Ansem interview: crypto bull case** — Ansem said he's never been more bullish on crypto, arguing fundamentals (rollups, Solana infra, regulatory clarity) are improving even as sentiment and price lag behind AI's dominance. [19:00]
- **AI + mobile enabling crypto apps** — Ansem argued AI makes building software easier for smaller teams who lack VC access, making crypto's permissionless liquidity more attractive, while mobile apps (Pump Fun, FOMO, X money) are finally bringing retail on-chain the way Robinhood/DraftKings do. [21:00]
- **L1 hype is dead, apps are the future** — Ansem said the 2020-2024 wave of L1 launches funded purely on speculation won't repeat; success now requires real apps with real usage, citing speculation/gamification (gotcha games, TCGs) and stablecoins as crypto's enduring strengths. [25:14]
- **Closing take** — Host said the show's crypto talk has picked up sharply as more on-chain activity (FWB, Robinhood chain, new tokens) resurfaces, framing the stream's mission as covering wherever money is being made across stocks, crypto and prediction markets. [33:12]

title: The Chinese Semiconductor Moment, Onchain Spots, and Celebrity Traders
summary:
The episode covered a hot on-chain/crypto market alongside stock earnings movement, semiconductor drama between the US and China, war escalation in multiple regions, and the ongoing fight over whether the Trump administration will restrict open-source AI.

- **Trader celebrity thesis** — Host revisited his take that traders/crypto speculators are becoming the next generation of celebrities, citing Ansem's huge Phantom wallet and Kimchi's viral 19M-view Twitter photo dump. [1:04]
- **Pump fun bullishness** — Host said he increased his pump fun position by 50% at the open, framing meme coins as a lasting cultural phenomenon, and noted crypto content flooding his TikTok feed. [3:22]
- **Market open recap** — SPX near all-time highs despite recent fear; semis (SOX, DRAM) weak; Bitcoin, hype, and pump fun strong; Nvidia and Cerebrus dropped notably, tied to China's ASML-related DUV chip news and a "long Eastern semis, short Western semis" trade idea. [6:54]
- **Strategy/MSTR news** — Michael Saylor's Strategy increased USD reserves by $500M and repurchased 300k shares of "stretch," pushing MSTR and stretch price up. [11:53]
- **War coverage** — Discussion of graphic Russia-Ukraine drone/train footage, Ukraine allegedly attacking an Iranian ship, and a Houthi attack on Saudi oil infrastructure, tied to concerns about the bond market (10-year yield) driving Trump's policy decisions. [17:19]
- **Open-source AI fight** — Coverage of the debate over whether Trump admin will ban open-source AI, featuring Jensen Huang's tweet defending open models and All In panel (Chamath, Sacks) arguing a ban would tank markets and accusing Anthropic of bad faith on distillation concerns. [20:04]
- **CXMT IPO** — Chinese memory maker CXMT's IPO traded huge volume on its first day, ballooning to a $500B valuation from an $85B deal, raising concerns about DRAM's future and possible US entity-list action. [27:13]
- **Political aside** — Brief mention that Kamala Harris may run again in 2028, with host predicting Marco Rubio or Gavin Newsom as stronger options. [29:21]

title: Why He Sold Everything - Bubble Boi on Kimi, CXMT, and China's Chips
summary:
A trader known as Bubble Boy returned to discuss his best-ever trading year, his shift to a net-short market stance, and how new AI developments are reshaping his views on chips, memory, and hyperscaler capex.

- **Best year ever** — Bubble Boy said his 2024 trading/consulting income has exceeded all his prior working years combined, crediting his engineering background for spotting real AI winners early. [1:08]
- **Nvidia dominance questioned** — He argued Nvidia's high margins invite hyperscalers to vertically integrate (own chips like TPUs/Trainium), meaning Nvidia's share of future compute may shrink even as the overall market grows. [4:51]
- **Memory and CXMT** — He explained Micron's HBM is lowest quality among major makers but that commodity DRAM (used to make HBM) is where the real price surge and profit is; he called China's CXMT DRAM IPO extremely cheap and said he'd try to get access. [7:02]
- **"Sold everything" tweet** — He referenced his viral July 17 tweet telling followers to sell everything, and said he's currently net short about 15% on SPX exposure, arguing institutional investors are locking in huge gains from AI stocks. [16:05]
- **Kimi and linear attention** — He detailed how Kimi's new "linear attention" technique gives AI models fixed memory size, which could cut DRAM demand but actually keeps GPUs busier, making it bullish for Nvidia despite fears about cheap Chinese open-source models. [19:56]
- **Google/Microsoft capex reaction** — He said markets punish rising capex short-term, but distinguished Google (justified by strong Gemini/AI products) from Microsoft (punished because its rental data-center strategy lacks a clear product story). [23:49]
- **Intel bullish, SMIC comparison dismissed** — He remains very bullish on Intel, citing prepaid customer commitments for its 14A node, and dismissed a SemiAnalysis report claiming SMIC beats Intel's 18A as a biased, incomplete comparison. [32:01]
- **Flash memory and Neoclouds as top trades** — He named Flash memory (citing Taiwan's Faison) as his top long idea to replace DRAM's role in AI systems, and said he's personally paying for Neocloud (Nebius) compute to run and test Kimi himself. [46:41]

title: Jensen Loves Open Source, Bubble Boi Shares Alpha, and I Have Fun Onchain
summary:
The episode covered market open coverage and a guest interview about AI/semiconductor trades.

- **Netflix and robotics chatter** — The hosts joked about a new Netflix prediction market show trailer and reacted with alarm to Unitree's latest sprinting robot dog video. [0:00]
- **YC crypto outlook** — They read from Y Combinator's request-for-startups document, noting its bullish stance on crypto rails, stablecoins, and tokenized stocks, and mentioned YC had funded Axie Infinity. [1:27]
- **Stock market open** — Major indices opened mixed (S&P flat, Nasdaq down 0.74%), with heavy selling in memory/semiconductor names like SK Hynix, Micron, and Cerebras, while Lockheed Martin extended a huge two-day rally and crypto (Bitcoin, Solana) dropped sharply. [3:33]
- **Iran escalation odds** — Polymarket odds on a US/Iran strike were cited as rising quickly (22% by the 25th, up to 55% by the 31st), alongside reports of US military assets massing in the Middle East. [9:53]
- **Bubble Boy's year** — Returning guest Bubble Boy said this has been his best trading year ever, crediting his engineering background and AI industry knowledge for spotting winners like Intel and SanDisk early. [11:37]
- **Nvidia moat debate** — Bubble Boy argued Nvidia's dominance and margins won't last forever since hyperscalers are incentivized to build their own chips (TPUs, Trainium), comparing it to being "beholden to one customer." [15:11]

title: The Leopold Aftermath, Ken Griffin's Playbook for Success, and Narrative Violations
summary:
The episode covered the fallout from Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness hedge fund losses, ran through market open with AI stocks bouncing back, and closed with the host announcing a week-long break.

- **Leopold aftermath** — The host noted there wasn't much fresh news on Aschenbrenner's fund blowup, just accumulating "lore," and predicted endless podcasts/articles will dissect it in time. [0:42]
- **Investor letter details** — Aschenbrenner's letter to LPs called the losses "expensive scars" and a learning experience; reports said the fund was down 67% in July but still up roughly 40-80% year-to-date, with the firm selling stock holdings to Citadel to raise cash for margin calls. [7:38]
- **Comparisons to past blowups** — The host compared the situation to Luna/3AC/FTX collapses in 2022, describing how confusing those were in real time and how "strong hands" tend to buy assets from forced sellers afterward. [4:05]
- **Confidence he'll return** — The host argued Aschenbrenner will easily raise money again despite the losses, comparing the dynamic (only half-seriously) to how eagerly people would fund Sam Bankman-Fried if he re-emerged. [9:06]
- **Market open rally** — Stocks opened strongly green (Nasdaq 100 up ~3%, semis up big, DRAM red at first then recovering) following a hot Korea session, though Apple and Amazon earnings reactions were volatile and Roblox dropped over 20% on a big miss. [12:01]
- **"Now what?" thesis** — The host argued the underlying problems behind the AI stock selloff (chip cost commoditization, China memory scares, rate uncertainty, lack of real productivity gains from AI) haven't been resolved even as prices bounce back euphorically. [14:47]
- **Rotation-to-crypto thesis and trades** — He floated a speculative idea that disillusionment with "AI as productive scam" could push money into direct speculation like Bitcoin and gold, said on-chain crypto feels exciting again, and mentioned having large personal positions in Pump Fun and another token (FWA). [17:44]
- **Sign-off** — The host wrapped up with advice on breaking into crypto/finance circles by being reliable rather than grinding "10,000 hours," announced Rhino would appear in a couple weeks, and confirmed he's heading off on a week-long vacation. [25:23]

title: Semiconductors Keep Crashing, Will the FOMC Save Us, and the Gatchafication of Everything
summary:
The episode covered pre-FOMC market jitters, a DRAM/KOSPI selloff, cultural riffs on collectibles and marijuana stats, a deep dive into the PayPal mafia, and Apple's new phone leasing program.

- **DRAM crash reaction** — The hosts opened discussing SK Hynix's earnings miss versus expectations, which sent DRAM down as much as 48% and the KOSPI down 6% in the prior session. [1:02]
- **FOMC setup** — They previewed the day's Fed decision, expecting no move but flagging a ~30% chance of hikes, and later read a tweet arguing forward guidance is ending, making future meetings more of a genuine 50/50 surprise again. [0:19]
- **Ad landscape and weed stat** — They complained that ads are now dominated by gambling and dating apps, and reacted to a headline that daily marijuana use has overtaken daily alcohol/tobacco use in the US, tying it (speculatively) to falling birth rates. [1:50]
- **Collectible-card bit and Gary Vee takes** — A joke "collectible card" segment (Madoff, SBF, Zuckerberg, Elizabeth Holmes) led into clips of Gary Vee arguing collectibles have replaced young people's interest in stocks and physical art, plus a bit about a $400 art purchase and the viral "Old Friend Photo Booth" business. [3:59]
- **Stock market open recap** — Market open was mixed/quiet ahead of FOMC: Nasdaq slightly green, Dow down about 1%, semis (SOX/SOXL) hit hard, crypto flat-to-down (BTC ~$64k), and a running joke about the "Shaws" token that had recently launched with no known founders. [14:08]
- **PayPal mafia deep dive** — Prompted by PayPal's earnings beat, they read through the full "PayPal mafia" roster — Thiel, Musk, Sacks, Levchin, Hoffman, the YouTube/Yelp/Reddit founders, and others — marveling at how many major companies trace back to it. [25:24]
- **Apple's leasing subscription** — They closed by discussing Apple's new "Apple Upgrade" leasing program for iPhones/Macs/Watches/iPads, questioning the economics and framing it as another step toward a "you'll own nothing" subscription economy. [30:29]

title: Ansem - Never Been This Bullish & the Billion Dollar Wallet
summary:
The episode is a wide-ranging interview with crypto trader Anom covering his bullish outlook on crypto, why he publicly calls market tops and bottoms, portfolio strategy, and how memecoins, onchain trading apps, and trader-celebrity culture are reshaping the space.

- **Historic crypto bullishness** — Anom explained his July tweet calling this his most bullish moment ever, arguing crypto fundamentals (rollups, Solana infra, regulation) are improving even as sentiment and price stay depressed, similar to Solana post-FTX in 2022. [3:54]
- **AI and mobile as crypto tailwinds** — He argued AI makes app-building cheaper for startups who then turn to crypto for instant liquidity, and that mobile trading apps (Pump Fun, Phantom, X Money) have massively improved access versus 2023's Unibot/Bonkbot era. [6:04]
- **Coinbase/BitMEX reflections** — Discussion of Brian Armstrong's relatability and Coinbase's dominance as other exchanges (Mt. Gox, Bitrix, BitMEX) faded, with BitMEX's decline tied to lax geo-blocking and lawsuits. [1:00]
- **Calling tops and bottoms publicly** — Anom explained why he likes making public bottom/top calls (helping followers, enjoying social media, being one of few willing to risk reputation), citing his bullish Solana call in 2023 as proof of concept. [18:24]
- **Portfolio allocation framework** — He laid out a rough split: ~20% cash, ~20% stocks, ~60% crypto right now, and within crypto 70% "safer" plays (majors plus a high-conviction midcap) versus 30% degen/onchain/perps trades. [37:54]
- **Memecoins and onchain culture as crypto's core draw** — He compared blockchains to cities needing both "banks" and "casinos," arguing memecoin/gambling culture (Pump Fun, TikTok trader virality like Kimchi) is a legitimate, not shameful, driver of crypto adoption. [1:03:30]
- **Traders as new celebrities** — Both discussed how traders differ from other celebrities because they can actually teach followers how they made money, fueling trading's growing mainstream/TikTok appeal. [58:56]
- **Stock market volatility and Bitcoin-as-gold thesis** — They discussed violent swings in stocks (Micron, SanDisk) resembling altcoin action, and floated the idea that Bitcoin could benefit as a scarce, AI-uncorrelated asset while AI-linked stocks whipsaw. [50:16]
